There is now code behind the roster's 'lint rejects any other'. workflow_problems rejects, in the hand-written region, a direct agent( call, any 'model:' or 'effort:' text, and any assignment to RUN.tier, TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE, and fixture tests pin each rule. But the rule is broader than the design and rejects what the design requires. The design's own story.js skeleton (topics/story-script.md lines 36 and 43: RUN.tier = a.tier || null; RUN.tier = s.config.tier_override || null) and wave.js skeleton (topics/wave-script.md line 31) set RUN.tier in the hand-written region. That is how the VSDD_TEST_TIER override from the survey reaches the step wrapper (conventions.md, topics/model-tiers.md). Running the lint over the extracted skeletons gives 'the tier settings are the roster's (... RUN.tier =)' for story and wave, and over both toy workflows. So W2, the next slice workflow, fails the lint if built as written. The regex scan also does not skip comments or strings: '// hand the agent (the implementer) its brief', a prompt string containing 'effort:', and a data key { model: u.model } are each rejected. To do: allow the design's tier-override adoption, either by moving it into a stamped prelude helper (for example adoptRun(s) / adoptParent(a)) so the hand-written region never assigns RUN.tier, or by allowing exactly the two forms the skeletons use. Strip // and /* */ comments and string literals before the agent( and model:/effort: scans. Add a test that the story and wave skeletons in the design pass workflow_problems.
